subject: math
cluster: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations

items.prompt: Solve the system by substitution: $\begin{cases} y = 2x - 1 \\ 3x + y = 9 \end{cases}$

steps: The first equation already gives $y = 2x - 1$, so substitute that into the second equation.
The solution is the ordered pair $(2, 3)$.

items.prompt: Solve the system by substitution: $\begin{cases} x = y + 4 \\ 2x + y = 11 \end{cases}$

steps: The first equation gives $x = y + 4$. Substitute this into the second equation.

items.prompt: Solve the system by elimination: $\begin{cases} x + y = 7 \\ x - y = 3 \end{cases}$

steps: The $y$ terms are already opposites, so add the two equations to eliminate $y$.

items.prompt: Determine the number of solutions of the system $\begin{cases} y = 4x + 1 \\ y = 4x - 5 \end{cases}$.

steps: Both equations are in slope-intercept form, so read the slope and intercept directly.
The first line has slope $4$ and $y$-intercept $1$; the second has slope $4$ and $y$-intercept $-5$.
Equal slopes but different $y$-intercepts means the lines are parallel and never meet.
Parallel distinct lines do not intersect, so the system has no solution.

items.prompt: Verify whether $(3, -1)$ is a solution of the system $\begin{cases} x + y = 2 \\ 2x - y = 7 \end{cases}$.

steps: A solution must satisfy both equations, so substitute $x = 3$ and $y = -1$ into each.
First equation: $x + y = 3 + (-1) = 2$, which matches $2$. True.
Second equation: $2x - y = 2(3) - (-1) = 6 + 1 = 7$, which matches $7$. True.
Since both equations are satisfied, $(3, -1)$ is a solution of the system.

items.prompt: Solve the system by substitution: $\begin{cases} 2x + y = 5 \\ 3x - 2y = 4 \end{cases}$
Solve the system by elimination: $\begin{cases} 3x + 2y = 16 \\ x - 2y = 0 \end{cases}$

steps: The $y$ terms are $+2y$ and $-2y$, which are opposites, so add the equations.

items.prompt: Solve the system by elimination, scaling one equation first: $\begin{cases} x + 3y = 9 \\ 2x - y = 4 \end{cases}$

steps: Multiply the first equation by $2$ so the $x$ coefficients match: $2x + 6y = 18$.
Subtract the second equation $2x - y = 4$ from this: $(2x + 6y) - (2x - y) = 18 - 4$.

items.prompt: Determine the number of solutions of the system $\begin{cases} 2x + 4y = 6 \\ x + 2y = 3 \end{cases}$.

steps: Compare the two equations to see if one is a multiple of the other.
This is exactly the first equation, so both equations describe the same line.
When two equations represent the same line, every point on the line works, so there are infinitely many solutions.
The $y$ terms are $+3y$ and $-3y$, which are opposites, so add the equations.

items.prompt: Solve the system by elimination, scaling both equations: $\begin{cases} 3x + 2y = 7 \\ 2x + 5y = 12 \end{cases}$

steps: To eliminate $x$, make the $x$ coefficients match. Multiply the first equation by $2$ and the second by $3$.
Subtract the first from the second: $(6x + 15y) - (6x + 4y) = 36 - 14$, giving $11y = 22$, so $y = 2$.

items.prompt: At a snack stand, hot dogs cost $\$3$ each and pretzels cost $\$2$ each. A customer buys $9$ items in all and spends $\$23$. How many hot dogs and how many pretzels did the customer buy?

steps: Let $h$ be the number of hot dogs and $p$ be the number of pretzels.
Solve the first equation for $p$: $p = 9 - h$.
Substitute into the cost equation: $3h + 2(9 - h) = 23$, so $3h + 18 - 2h = 23$.
The customer bought $5$ hot dogs and $4$ pretzels.

items.prompt: A theater sells adult tickets for $\$11$ and student tickets for $\$7$. One evening it sells $200$ tickets and collects $\$1840$. Find the number of adult tickets $a$ and student tickets $s$, then find how many more student tickets than adult tickets were sold.
items.answer: $110$ adult and $90$ student tickets; $20$ fewer student tickets than adult, i.e. the difference $s - a = -20$.

steps: Let $a$ be adult tickets and $s$ be student tickets.
Subtract this from the money equation: $(11a + 7s) - (7a + 7s) = 1840 - 1400$, giving $4a = 440$, so $a = 110$.
The requested difference is $s - a = 90 - 110 = -20$, meaning $20$ fewer student tickets than adult tickets were sold.

items.prompt: For what value of $k$ does the system $\begin{cases} y = 3x + 5 \\ y = kx - 2 \end{cases}$ have no solution?

steps: A linear system has no solution when the two lines are parallel: equal slopes but different $y$-intercepts.
The first line has slope $3$; the second line has slope $k$.
Check the intercepts: the first has intercept $5$ and the second has intercept $-2$, which are different, so the lines are parallel and distinct.

items.prompt: A chemist mixes a $10\%$ acid solution with a $25\%$ acid solution to make $30$ liters of a $20\%$ acid solution. Let $x$ be the liters of $10\%$ solution and $y$ the liters of $25\%$ solution. How many liters of each are needed?
items.answer: $10$ liters of the $10\%$ solution and $20$ liters of the $25\%$ solution

steps: Multiply the acid equation by $100$ to clear decimals: $10x + 25y = 600$.
From the volume equation, $x = 30 - y$. Substitute: $10(30 - y) + 25y = 600$.
Use $10$ liters of the $10\%$ solution and $20$ liters of the $25\%$ solution.
